visuals.heading: Key Ideas at a Glance

items.text: Yes, law is a good career field in India, but treat it as six different branches with very different pay and daily work, not one job.

blocks.heading: Law Remains a Genuinely Viable, In-Demand Field

items.text: But "good career" does not mean "any LLB, any college, guaranteed courtroom glamour or corporate riches."

It means: real demand exists in specific, well-defined branches, real pay exists for graduates who build deliberately toward those branches, and a genuinely uneven, sometimes brutal, first few years exist too, especially for the litigation path most families default to imagining when they hear "law."
Before comparing pay, it helps to see the actual shape of the field, because "lawyer" as a single job title genuinely undersells how many different careers a law degree opens.

The order below is deliberate, not alphabetical or prestige-based: litigation and corporate/in-house lead because they carry this field's strongest real growth and growth headroom, litigation through a genuine scalable-ownership path once you build your own practice or chamber, corporate and in-house work through the fastest-growing early-career pay ceiling of any branch.
Arguing in court, drafting pleadings, and building a practice under a senior advocate.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: A generic salary number pulled from a Tier-1 firm's recruiting page, or a relative's opinion that "law is a respectable, safe profession," will not tell you whether this field actually fits your money, your patience, and your target branch.
Law rewards people who can read dense, precise language for hours without losing focus, and who can hold a client's or a judge's attention while explaining something complicated in plain terms.
If the appeal is mainly courtroom drama from television, that is a signal to test the litigation branch specifically before committing five years and a real fee to the whole field.

blocks.heading: Spend Money and Time on This

items.text: The four questions tells you whether law fits on paper.
Do not lock in a law college seat before passing all three proofs.
Write one real research memo or case note on an actual legal issue, not a generic "why I want to study law" essay.

blocks.heading: How to Actually Raise Your Income Ceiling

items.text: This field's income ceiling is not fixed by which college you attended; it is set by how deliberately you move from a generic legal credential toward a specific, scarce combination of skills.

The clearest ceiling-raising moves here are: building a genuine sector specialisation, data protection, fintech regulation, IP and patent work, competition law, once basic legal training and one or two strong internships exist; moving from a generalist litigation practice toward a specific court or subject-matter reputation; moving from a corporate firm associate role toward in-house leadership or independent advisory work once a real client network forms; and, for graduates who combine law with another degree, engineering plus IP, commerce plus tax, building a niche few pure-law graduates can match.
None of these are guaranteed outcomes, and none happen from the degree alone.
Graduates who spend five years without testing litigation, corporate, or policy work through internships often leave college with a strong CV and no real sense of which lane actually fits them.

Since the Supreme Court restored the mandatory three-year practice requirement in May 2025, a fresh graduate can no longer sit most state judicial service exams straight out of college in the way earlier batches could.
In most states, document review and contract-lifecycle work at an LPO does not count as court practice for the new three-year rule.

blocks.heading: Real Pay, But a New Practice-First Rule

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: A Civil Judge (Junior Division) starts on a basic pay of roughly Rs 77,840 a month, with gross monthly pay commonly landing between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 1.45 lakh once dearness allowance, house rent allowance, and judicial allowances are added. That is a genuinely strong, government-scale starting income, and one of very few defined-benefit career ladders left in the legal field.

blocks.heading: Corporate Law Firms Vs In-House Counsel

figures.label: Entry Level Pay
figures.source: Tier-1 firm associate life, roughly Rs 15-22.5 LPA at the fresher level at firms like Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, AZB & Partners, Khaitan & Co, Trilegal, Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas, and JSA, comes with genuinely long hours during live deals. The highest-paying teams inside these firms in 2026 are mergers and acquisitions, private equity, capital markets, competition law, and banking and finance, the transactional groups billing the largest deals.

visuals.heading: Why This Question Needs a Field-Level Answer

items.text: Pay ranges across these branches do not overlap much at entry level: a first-year litigation junior and a first-year Tier-1 firm associate can be earning ten to fifteen times apart.

Regulation is reshaping the field mid-career for current students, the judiciary's 2025 practice-first rule and the Bar Council's still-developing AI-conduct rules both changed the ground rules in the last two years.

Unlike medicine or CA, there is no single unifying licensing exam entry requirement at the very start; AIBE and state bar enrolment matter for practice, but several branches, in-house, LPO, policy, academia, do not strictly require them at all.

blocks.heading: Actually Changing in Law Right Now

items.text: High-volume document review and first-pass due diligence in M&A, real estate, and litigation discovery, now standard AI-assisted work at most mid-to-large firms and LPOs.
Boilerplate contract drafting and clause-matching against a standard template.
Summarising case law and statutes for a first-draft research memo.

blocks.heading: What to Tell a Worried Family

items.text: Fear that "law" only means courtroom work, with the well-known uncertainty of early litigation income.
Stories about junior lawyers struggling financially in the first few years.
Not knowing whether an NLU seat, a private college, or a 3-year route after another degree matters most for a specific target branch.
